title: How many generators can arrive?

blocks.text: A generator rental firm keeps portable generators in yards and sends them to towns after a storm. Before the season it asks how many generators its road routes could deliver at most.

Write `most_delivered(stock, needs, routes)` in `generators.py`, using `SimpleMaxFlow`. `stock` maps each yard to the generators it holds, `needs` maps each town to the most it can take, and `routes` maps `(from, to)` pairs of place names to the most generators that route carries. A route may pass through a place that is neither a yard nor a town. Return the largest number that can arrive at the towns in total.
The problem, with a super source $`s`$ joined to every yard and a super sink $`t`$ joined from every town:
The solver writes the rows; you give it the arcs. Number the places first (`SimpleMaxFlow` knows nodes only as integers), and give the super source and sink numbers after them. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from generators import most_delivered

# Generator units: yard stock, town needs, and route capacities.
stock = {"East yard": 8, "West yard": 6}
needs = {"Fen": 7, "Glen": 9}
routes = {("East yard", "Hub"): 6, ("Hub", "Fen"): 3, ("Hub", "Glen"): 5,
          ("East yard", "Fen"): 2, ("West yard", "Glen"): 4}
print("units delivered:", most_delivered(stock, needs, routes))
print("units delivered, Glen needs 2:", most_delivered(stock, dict(needs, Glen=2), routes))
print("units delivered, West yard holds 1:", most_delivered(dict(stock, **{"West yard": 1}), needs, routes))

cases.says: when every yard and town has room, the routes' capacities decide what arrives
a yard sends no more than its stock, however wide its routes
a town takes no more than it needs, however wide the routes into it
units may travel through a place that is neither a yard nor a town

origin.section: Many Sources and Many Sinks Become One Pair With a Super Source and a Super Sink

concepts: SimpleMaxFlow takes integer-numbered nodes and arcs with capacities, solves from a source to a sink, and reports a minimum cut
several sources and sinks are joined to one super source and one super sink by arcs as wide as each stock and need
